titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 13/2008 (އެންޓި-ކޮރަޕްޝަން ކޮމިޝަނުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Anti-Corruption Commission Act (Act No. 13/2008). It replaces Article 7, which is about how the Commission's president and vice-president are appointed, with a new three-part version. It also deletes sub-articles (c) and (d) of Article 10 and sub-article (c) of Article 11, and replaces sub-article (c) of Article 15. A short transitional clause covers how the changes apply to people already in office. The scans are hard to read, so some details are uncertain.
whyItMatters: If passed, the rules for who leads the Anti-Corruption Commission, and how those posts are filled, would change for future appointments.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 replaces Article 7 (the article on appointing the Commission's president and vice-president) with new sub-articles (a), (b) and (c). The exact wording could not be read reliably.
Clause 2 deletes sub-articles (c) and (d) of Article 10.
Clause 4 replaces sub-article (c) of Article 15 with a new text.
Clause 5 is a transitional provision on how the new Article 7 applies to people already holding the posts.
Clause 6 says when the law takes effect, which appears to be on ratification. A table at the end of the bill sets the old and new wording of each article side by side.
whoIsAffected: The Anti-Corruption Commission's president, vice-president and members, and the people who appoint or approve them.
statedReasons: The explanatory note says the bill is submitted to amend the Anti-Corruption Commission Act (No. 13/2008). The scan is too hard to read for the full reasons.
